correctness.rationale: In a reversible eigenbasis, the finite-K scalar multiplier is exact. Its numerator is positive for all nonnegative eigenvalues and all even K, and for odd K has exactly one possible negative-eigenvalue zero; this proves all lower bounds even under adaptive choices on generic inputs. K=1 kills each negative distinct mode in one epoch. A nonedge gives a nonnegative second eigenvalue by a 2x2 principal submatrix and Cauchy interlacing. The provided checker passed 15 regular graph types/360 filter comparisons plus an exact rational three-node rank-one product. The analytic proof, not finite experiments, supplies the universal theorem.

value.rationale: A recent predictive-loop opinion model motivates an exact question that its equilibrium analysis does not address: can an operator force unanimity in finitely many platform cycles using longer peer exposure? The complete criterion shows exactly when this is possible, gives the sharp count of necessary outer rounds, and proves extra finite peer rounds cannot help. The structural nonedge barrier contrasts sharply with general finite-time consensus on sparse graphs and prevents a tempting but invalid intervention strategy.
